title: RAW UNREVIEWED: flower removal changes the fruit outcome for one owned plant
summary: Source-first causal contrast for the unresolved chor/shor flower-versus-fruit direction. Find a pre-1450 primary instruction that explicitly retains one identified plant, removes its flowers in one branch, leaves comparable flowers intact in another, and gives opposed later fruit or seed outcomes. Freeze the source's plant, intervention, timing, and outcome before any admitted Voynich text is read. Only a separately established target word or panel owner for the same intervention and outcome could distinguish chor=flower/shor=fruit from the reverse. A mere seasonal flower-to-fruit sequence, shared spelling, plant illustration, or generic harvest passage is insufficient. No source or target binding has yet been found; no target is nominated and the idea is not selected for testing.

design.mechanism: Causal flower-removal versus intact-flower branches with one retained plant identity and opposed later fruit or seed outcomes
design.unit: One complete pre-1450 source-owned plant instruction and, only after independent ownership, a complete admitted nonreserved manuscript record
design.contrast: chor=flower and shor=fruit versus the reverse, plus a nonreproductive inventory reading
design.prediction: A fixed whole reading must assign removal to the independently owned flower term and loss of later fruit to the independently owned fruit term in the same plant case; reversed and inventory readings predict different participants or no causal outcome. Without two independent term bindings the alternatives remain tied.
